title: Development data table, UNDP and World Bank figures with years
subject: Geography
source: Written for geography/y9 lesson 15 (Development data table, UNDP and World Bank figures with years (portal printable))
intro: Lesson 15: How is development measured? GDP, HDI and life expectancy. Read the ideas from the lesson, then do the tasks.

model.title: Compare the HDI of the UK and Malawi. (2 marks)

parts.text: The UK's is nearly twice as high: longer lives, more schooling, higher income (1)

keywords.def: the value of goods and services produced, divided by population
Human Development Index, combining health, education and income
the average number of years a person is expected to live
a measure used to show something
the percentage of adults who can read and write

questions.q: Give one weakness of GDP per capita as an indicator. (2 marks)
questions.a: It is an average (1), so it hides inequality between rich and poor (1)

questions.q: Core: Use the data table (UK, India, Malawi: HDI, life expectancy, GDP per capita, literacy) to draw one bar chart and write three comparison sentences with data.
Extend: Explain why HDI is better than GDP alone.
questions.a: It includes health and education, not just income

questions.q: Stretch: Suggest one thing HDI leaves out.

questions.a: B) Income. HDI uses life expectancy, schooling and income.

questions.q: Life expectancy is an example of a:
Big question: can one number show how good life is?
questions.a: No single number can; HDI is better as it combines several, but still hides inequality
